extracts.lead_summary: A flat week that was anything but. XLC closed $110.38 (+0.05%) — six cents from where it started — after SpaceX agreed on Thursday night to pay a reported $8 billion for a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio and said it intends to be a major mobile carrier. On Friday T-Mobile fell 13.3%, AT&T 9.8%, Verizon 8.7%, Charter 5.7%, Comcast 2.6%; three of the five closed at 52-week lows and the carriers traded four times their normal volume. The fund gave up 1.5% that day and still finished the week even, because Alphabet rose 2.4%, Netflix 4.8%, Disney 5.7% and Take-Two 5.3% over the four days before. The barbell I keep describing just had one end sawn off. A sector where a Thursday-night press release can take 9–13% out of three dividend stocks is not a defensive sector, and the yield sleeve I had at underweight is now the thing I was underweight for.
